Also cannot be adjacent diagonally: meaning queens cannot be in positions that are diagonally adjacent (difference in row and column both 1). But rule 2 says: "Queens may not touch, including diagonally. Thus queens in consecutive rows cannot occupy columns differing by 1. Queens separated by more than one row MAY share a long diagonal; this is not the ordinary chess N-queens diagonal rule." So adjacency includes horizontal, vertical, diagonal adjacency. Also queens separated by more than one row may share a long diagonal; that's allowed. So we don't need to enforce standard N-queens diagonal constraints.
